chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Shajarah, from some of the companions of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you recite 'Tabbat Yadu Abi Lahab' and 'Tab', supplicate against Abu Lahab, for he was among those who denied, who denied the Prophet (peace be upon him) and what he brought from Allah, the Exalted and Glorious.

key_terms.الْمُكَذِّبِينَ: The deniers, specifically those who rejected the truth.
key_terms.تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ: The opening phrase of Surah Al-Lahab, meaning 'May the hands of Abu Lahab perish'.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: The Exalted and Glorious (attributes of Allah).

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be made when reciting Surah Al-Lahab?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* establishes a specific ritual link between reciting Surah Al-Lahab and invoking divine curse (*du'a*) against Abu Lahab, emphasizing his role as an archetypal denier of prophethood. In Shia tradition, this practice underscores the theological significance of *al-Ghuluw* (extremity in denial) and serves as a means of aligning oneself with the Prophet’s enemies to gain spiritual reward. The instruction highlights the interplay between Quranic recitation and supplicatory action, reinforcing the concept of *Tawalla* (affiliation with the faithful) and *Tabarra* (disavowal of enemies) through the lens of Surah Al-Lahab.
